text: Why we built it
textPreview: Why we built it

text:
NILM estimates appliance activity from one aggregate measurement at the point of common coupling.
The practical challenge is overlap: several devices run at once, similar loads share the same P range, and PV can mask consumption by driving signed power toward zero.
The project therefore uses every measurable low-frequency signature: active/reactive power, power factor, THD, per-order harmonics and switching edges.

text: Data path
textPreview: Data path

text:
Synthetic generator: eight appliance models plus baseload, PV and four-quadrant machine behavior; exact per-sample ground truth.
Aggregator: phase-wise P/Q summation, synthesized voltage/frequency, and complex vector summation of current harmonics (orders 2-40).
PAC4200 reader: persistent Modbus TCP acquisition, 5 Hz samples, session recorder, harmonic file-record probing and HDF5 output.
Measured scenario mixer: loops real single-device recordings with random ON/OFF schedules to create labelled multi-device training mixes.

text: Edge detection in detail
textPreview: Edge detection in detail

text:
The live engine scans the last 8 s of P/Q samples and compares settled medians before and after the strongest jump.
An edge counts only above thresholds (about 8 W or 16 var), after quiet-state checks and a debounce interval.
Each edge is matched to single-device signatures in dP/dQ space; matched edges claim devices ON/OFF with exact timestamps.
Residual power is not forced into known classes: sustained unexplained power triggers the unknown-device teaching workflow.

text: Training-on-the-go
textPreview: Training-on-the-go

text:
1. Unknown residual appears in the live dashboard.
2. User names the device and records an isolated OFF-ON-OFF sequence.
3. Measured scenarios are rebuilt automatically.
4. Mix and identify models retrain in the background and hot-reload.
5. New device vocabulary is stored in the model bundle; no code change is required.

text: What worked
textPreview: What worked

text:
End-to-end loop works: record, mix, train, infer, run live, detect unknowns and retrain.
Event features improved the measured-data mix model compared with the earlier frozen bundle.
The live monitor combines RF window predictions with edge claims, so fast switching information is not lost inside 10 s windows.

text: What can be improved
textPreview: What can be improved

text:
Record real PV during actual generation; current PV recordings contain almost no generated power.
Measure several sessions per device and more variants of small fans, then use grouped evaluation by session.
Run feature ablations: common vs harmonic, 14 vs 17 aggregate features, and with/without edge features.
Use sequence models (CNN/LSTM or seq2point) for long appliance cycles such as washing machines.
Validate on true simultaneous multi-device recordings, not only semi-synthetic measured mixes.

text: Conclusion
textPreview: Conclusion

text: A 5 Hz industrial power meter is enough for a useful NILM laboratory system when its processed channels are fused deliberately. The current implementation is not just an offline classifier: it is a deployable workflow with measured data ingestion, RF presence/power inference, edge-aware live events, residual honesty and guided learning for unknown loads.

text: Evaluation protocol
textPreview: Evaluation protocol

text:
Mix model: grouped held-out split over measured scenarios, ON threshold 5 W.
Metrics travel with the model bundle: feature list, appliance vocabulary, F1 and MAE.
Real mixed recordings without per-sample ground truth are evaluated as expected device sets parsed from filenames.
The poster reports tracked metrics from output/train_mix_metrics.json and output/train_identify_metrics.json.
